Note::replace_first¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::replace_first(std::string_view from, std::string_view to) const

Substitute Only The First Occurrence¶

replace_first(from, to) returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with the leftmost occurrence of the literal string from in each cell rewritten to to. Later occurrences are left untouched. It is the bounded sibling of replace (which rewrites all) and the substitute-form of remove.

Use it when a token is expected once, or when only the first hit is meaningful — a leading label, the first field separator, the first of a series you will handle one at a time.

Edge cases¶

  • An empty from is a no-op — the cell is returned unchanged.

  • A from that does not occur leaves the cell unchanged.

  • An empty to deletes the first from; that is exactly remove(from).

The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note.

Example 1: First Match Only¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"alpha beta beta gamma", "beta", "no match"})
        .replace_first("beta", "X"))
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["alpha X beta gamma", "X", "no match"]

Example 2: An Empty from Is A No-Op¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::make_note({"abc"}).replace_first("", "X");
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["abc"]

Example 3: No Match Leaves The Cell Unchanged¶

pluss::note::print(std::cout, pluss::make_note({"abc"}).replace_first("z", "X"))
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["abc"]

See Also¶

  • Note::replace: rewrite all occurrences.

  • Note::replace_last: rewrite only the rightmost.

  • Note::replace_n: rewrite the first n.

  • Note::remove: replace_first(from, "").
